items.prompt: Your app's `Storage` interface has `put(key, bytes)`. The new cloud SDK offers `upload_object(bucket, name, stream, metadata)`. Your code should keep calling `put`.
items.why: Incompatible interface you must fit into yours → Adapter.

items.prompt: An HTTP client should optionally get retries, request logging and response caching, in any combination per call site, without a subclass for each combination.
items.why: Stackable add-ons with the same interface → Decorator.

items.prompt: A bundle of products is priced as the sum of its items, and bundles can contain other bundles. The cart should call `price()` without checking what kind of item it holds.
items.why: Part-whole tree treated uniformly → Composite. Polymorphism (oop-basics) is the mechanism, but the recursive group structure is the pattern.

items.prompt: Each incoming support ticket goes first to a bot, then to tier-1, then to tier-2. Whoever can solve it stops it there.
items.why: 'Whoever can handle it stops it' → Chain of responsibility. A decorator would always pass the call along.

items.prompt: A high-resolution map tile is expensive to load. The UI holds tile objects for the whole map, but each one should load its pixels only when first drawn.
items.why: Same interface, delays creation of the real subject until first use → virtual Proxy. Not a creational factory: the caller already holds the object.

items.prompt: The checkout controller calls inventory, pricing, payment, shipping and email in a fixed order, and three other controllers copy the same sequence.
items.why: One simple entry point over a subsystem of many classes → Facade (which also removes the duplication).

items.prompt: The team argues whether `SearchService` should inherit from `ElasticClient` to reuse its methods, or hold one as a field.
items.why: The question is the principle itself, composition over inheritance. No specific pattern is being asked for.
